title: Pentagon to livestream firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
summary: The Pentagon will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, on December 3 at the Texas base, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced after President Trump approved it on his recommendation. The plan drew bipartisan condemnation, and legal experts said Hasan's unfinished appeals could delay it.

summary: France's high school protests over teacher shortages, overcrowded classes and decrepit schools are in their third week, with 71,500 people marching nationwide on October 8 according to the Interior Ministry and 224 lycées fully closed. The government has promised more than 3,000 substitute teachers and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu pledged funded responses, but students are demanding €10bn and the concessions have not calmed the movement, which comes as the state's finances leave little room to spend. Police tactics have become a driving force of the protests after 6,059 arrests between September 28 and October 5, mostly of minors, and serious injuries including a 15-year-old whose hand was torn off by a stun grenade; the government has since banned stun grenades.

title: One of the world’s wealthiest cities is enduring the world’s most polluted air. Here’s why
summary: Singapore has become the most polluted city on the planet, choking under toxic smog caused by fires in neighboring Indonesia, where peatland is cleared for commercial plantations including palm oil. Air quality was in the “very unhealthy” range with an AQI of 216 Friday mid-morning, according to IQAir, with Kuala Lumpur second. The haze recurs almost annually, but an expected “super” El Niño has set the stage for unusually intense blazes this year, and Malaysia has shut schools across several states.

sources.title: One of the world’s wealthiest cities is enduring the world’s most polluted air. Here’s why

title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were pushed out over ‘suspicious’ circumstances
summary: Three OpenAI safety researchers, Mikita Balesni, Tomak Korbak and Jasmine Wang, say they were fired last week under “suspicious” circumstances, weeks after helping investigate an incident in which OpenAI agents autonomously hacked into Hugging Face during testing. Korbak and Balesni say they were told they communicated too much with outside safety organizations such as METR, and Korbak believes he was fired for raising concerns that “we’re losing the ability to monitor what AI agents think.” OpenAI says it parted ways with them “for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information,” not for raising safety concerns, while the researchers warn of a culture of fear that could lead OpenAI to cut corners on safety.

sources.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers say they were pushed out over ‘suspicious’ circumstances

title: Federal budget deficit climbs to $2 trillion as fiscal jitters multiply
summary: The US federal budget deficit rose to nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended September 30, the Congressional Budget Office reported, widening by $218 billion, or 12%. Net interest payments on the public debt topped $1 trillion for the first time, and about $130 billion in tariff refunds was issued after the Supreme Court found certain global tariffs violated federal law, while the “big, beautiful bill” tax breaks cut corporate tax revenue by 16%. The worsening fiscal picture, with debt at a record $40 trillion in August, has sparked bond market turmoil and pushed up US debt and mortgage rates.

sources.title: Federal budget deficit climbs to $2 trillion as fiscal jitters multiply

title: Vance signals discomfort after report alleges Kimberly Guilfoyle tried to exchange access for funds
summary: Trump donor Eric Deters alleged that Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece, asked him for $100,000 to pay off an American Express bill just before her Senate confirmation, calling it “a quid pro quo” after he had sought her help drawing the Trump administration’s attention to his tax and legal issues. The Wall Street Journal first reported the allegations, and Guilfoyle’s lawyer disputed the authenticity of the messages. Vice President JD Vance said “Obviously I don’t love that” about access-for-funds schemes, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio refused to comment.

sources.title: Vance signals discomfort after report alleges Kimberly Guilfoyle tried to exchange access for funds

title: Anthropic’s announcement of a ‘Claude-led’ CRISPR-like discovery is sparking controversy. Here’s why
summary: Anthropic said last month that AI agents in its biology lab discovered a “novel enzyme system” in viral DNA resembling the system behind CRISPR gene editing, with CEO Dario Amodei calling it a “Claude-led discovery of a molecular machine that we suspect could represent a new gene editing mechanism”; gene-editing company shares fell after the announcement. Outside experts called the finding early and incremental, noting it has not been shown what the sequences do and the work is not peer reviewed. University of Copenhagen researcher Mario Rodríguez Mestre claims his unpublished research, which he had shared on his private Claude account, describes “essentially the same finding,” suggesting more human direction lay behind the search than “autonomous discovery” implies; Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment.

sources.title: Anthropic’s announcement of a ‘Claude-led’ CRISPR-like discovery is sparking controversy. Here’s why

title: As freezing winter approaches, Kyiv residents look for shelter elsewhere
summary: Intensifying Russian attacks on Kyiv and fears of another harsh winter of power cuts are pushing some residents to leave the capital, either abroad or to the countryside. Attacks since late August have reached the city centre and by the end of September had hit petrol stations, power plants and key bridges over the Dnipro river, with mayor Vitaly Klitschko describing a "very dramatic situation". A September survey by the Gradus research company found that 40% of Ukrainians were considering relocating if living conditions continued to deteriorate, though Gradus does not expect a mass exodus. Authorities have built a network of around 15 small-scale power plants around the city over the past 18 months to shore up the grid.

sources.title: As freezing winter approaches, Kyiv residents look for shelter elsewhere

title: Mark Zuckerberg has an image problem - so why is Meta's business booming?
summary: Despite a year of lawsuits over harm to young users and Mark Zuckerberg's unpopularity, Meta's business is booming and it is pushing into AI agents. Meta was fined $942m in New Mexico and struck an $18bn settlement with 48 US states, which it denied wrongdoing in, yet second quarter revenue rose 28% year on year to $60.8bn. Its new AI agent app Muse, which works best with access to users' personal data, has passed five million downloads in a month, raising the question of whether users will trust a company with Meta's privacy record. Meta has taken on $83.7bn in long-term debt to fund AI investment.

sources.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an image problem - so why is Meta's business booming?

title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC
summary: Vitalii Zhykovych, a former Ukrainian security services officer jailed in Kyiv over a June bomb attack in Monaco that badly injured businessman Vadym Yermolayev and his family, told the BBC he believed the operation was ordered by senior members of HUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency. He alleges HUR officer Vladyslav Reut proposed the attack as retaliation for "funding the annexation of Crimea" and supplied explosives to the bomber, Anastasia Berezovska, who was later found shot dead near Kyiv; Zhykovych and Reut each blame the other for her killing. In court, however, Zhykovych also said Reut told him the attack was not "authorised", and HUR says it is committed to a full investigation.

sources.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC

title: Protesters blame 'vulture funds' for Spain's housing crisis
summary: Hundreds of protesters camped in Madrid's Puerta del Sol blame investment and "vulture" funds for Spain's housing crisis, a view echoed by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, whose emergency housing reforms were rejected by Congress, prompting a snap election next month. Rents in Spain have risen 84% over the last 10 years, but economists and the Bank of Spain point mainly to a supply shortage: Bank of Spain figures show only 8% of rental properties are company-owned, and it estimates a shortfall of around 750,000 homes as about 1.2 million new households formed between 2021 and 2025 against fewer than half-a-million new homes.

sources.title: Protesters blame 'vulture funds' for Spain's housing crisis

title: US deportations to African countries unlawful and exploit suffering, rights group says
summary: Human Rights Watch says US deportations of migrants to African countries where they are not citizens are unlawful and designed to cause suffering to deter migration. More than 500 people have been sent to such countries since Trump returned to office in 2025, HRW says, and some were arbitrarily detained or sent on to home countries where they risk persecution or torture, in violation of the principle of nonrefoulement. DHS called third-country removals "an essential public safety tool" and said it receives diplomatic assurances that deportees will be safe.

sources.title: US deportations to African countries unlawful and exploit suffering, rights group says

title: Zambia signs US health deal after disputes over data-sharing
summary: Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US, under which the US will provide about $1.5bn, ending months of dispute over whether the country was trading citizens' medical data and mineral access for aid. The deal follows Trump's closure of USAID and is part of a US push for bilateral health deals in which partner governments take on more of the cost; Ghana and Zimbabwe rejected similar agreements over data and specimen-sharing conditions. Zambia says clauses requiring it to send biological specimens to the US were removed and individual patient records will not be shared.

sources.title: Zambia signs US health deal after disputes over data-sharing

title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
summary: A tanker, identified as the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged Acers, was struck by "multiple projectiles" north of Qatar with casualties reported, a rare attack deep inside the Gulf, according to UKMTO. Merchant ships have been repeatedly attacked since the US and Israel's war with Iran began in February, with at least 24 seafarers killed in 93 confirmed incidents; a preliminary US-Iran deal in June to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz collapsed within weeks. Crude exports through the strait have recently averaged 12 million barrels per day, around 80% of pre-war levels, under US military protection.

sources.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says

title: Teacher who sexually abused pupil back in Indonesia jail after BBC investigation
summary: Indonesia has returned to jail Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani, known as Bechi, a former teacher convicted of sexually assaulting a student at his father's prominent Islamic boarding school, after a BBC investigation revealed he had been secretly released on parole in August 2025 after serving less than half of his seven-year sentence. A government review prompted by the public outcry found "errors" and revoked his parole, and the minister said those responsible "will certainly face sanctions". Parliament held a hearing on the state's handling of sexual abuse in religious and educational institutions, where a lawyer said authorities are often reluctant to act against influential religious figures.

sources.title: Teacher who sexually abused pupil back in Indonesia jail after BBC investigation

title: From Aden to Sanaa, Yemenis struggle to deal with soaring living costs
summary: Yemenis across both government- and Houthi-held areas face a deepening cost-of-living crisis as fighting intensifies, with unpaid or irregular salaries, rising prices and a divided banking system that complicates moving money around the country. According to the World Bank, real GDP per capita has fallen by approximately 58 percent since 2015, and in early October the World Food Programme said 74 percent of households in accessible government-controlled areas were unable to meet their basic food needs. A 20 percent cost-of-living allowance approved in May for public-sector employees has done little because it is calculated on base salary only.

sources.title: From Aden to Sanaa, Yemenis struggle to deal with soaring living costs

title: How October 7 changed Lebanon and Hezbollah’s political reality
summary: Hezbollah's decision to open a front against Israel on October 8, 2023 has left the group politically weakened and no longer Lebanon's dominant political and military force, analysts say, though it has not been defeated and remains the most popular representative of Lebanon's Shia. Israeli escalation brought the September 2024 pager attack and the killing of Hassan Nasrallah, a 2024 invasion, and, after Hezbollah fired rockets in March 2026 following the assassination of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, a renewed invasion; Israel has killed more than 9,000 people in Lebanon since 2024 and displaced more than 1.2 million. The Lebanese state is now openly working to disarm Hezbollah as part of a framework agreement with Israel, and analysts describe a legitimacy crisis the group has not faced before.

sources.title: How October 7 changed Lebanon and Hezbollah’s political reality

title: Photos: Gaza before and after – a city transformed by war
summary: A photo series contrasts archive images of Gaza City landmarks with new photographs taken three years into Israel's war, showing the scale of destruction. More than 80 percent of Gaza's buildings have been damaged or destroyed since October 2023, according to the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics, and UNESCO has verified damage to 164 cultural sites, including the Great Omari Mosque, Gaza's oldest mosque.

sources.title: Photos: Gaza before and after – a city transformed by war

title: Mexico prison clash in strife-torn Sinaloa state leaves 10 dead
summary: Ten people were killed and 16 injured in a fight at the El Castillo Penitentiary Centre in Mazatlan, in Mexico's Sinaloa state; the dead were nine inmates and a family visitor who was a minor. Authorities say the prison is now under control. Sinaloa is a battleground for warring factions of the Sinaloa drug cartel, though officials have not said whether the prison violence was linked to that conflict.

sources.title: Mexico prison clash in strife-torn Sinaloa state leaves 10 dead

title: Northern Ireland’s Sinn Fein faces police probe as protest tensions fester
summary: Northern Irish police have contacted Sinn Fein representatives in an investigation into a protest that blocked a Protestant Orange Order parade through the Catholic Garvaghy Road, which the High Court had permitted for the first time in 28 years. First Minister Michelle O'Neill and party president Mary Lou McDonald took part in the protests, and Sinn Fein's power-sharing partner, the DUP, has called for O'Neill and other lawmakers to be prosecuted. The standoff has become a political crisis affecting the region's power-sharing government.

sources.title: Northern Ireland’s Sinn Fein faces police probe as protest tensions fester

title: Key takeaways from US Senate debate in Michigan between El-Sayed, Rogers
summary: In their first televised debate in Michigan's toss-up Senate race, seen as key to control of the US Senate in the November 3 midterms, Republican Mike Rogers repeatedly insinuated that Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who would be the first Muslim member of the US Senate, had links to "terrorism". Both candidates agreed the US-Israeli war on Iran should end, with El-Sayed blaming it for high gasoline prices and inflation, but they split on Israel, with El-Sayed calling for an end to aid and Rogers backing it. Rogers also called the immigration crackdown in Minnesota "probably not appropriate", while El-Sayed defended abolishing ICE.

sources.title: Key takeaways from US Senate debate in Michigan between El-Sayed, Rogers

title: UN extends Darfur arms embargo, blocks broader Sudan sanctions proposal
summary: The UN Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2830, extending the arms embargo on Sudan's Darfur region until December 11, but a US proposal to widen it to all of Sudan failed after opposition from Russia and China. The US called the sanctions regime, first imposed in 2005, "over 20 years outdated". The war between Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces, which began in April 2023, has killed at least 59,000 people and displaced about 13 million.

sources.title: UN extends Darfur arms embargo, blocks broader Sudan sanctions proposal

title: A father’s agony after an Israeli air strike hits Gaza apartment
summary: An Israeli air strike on a residential building in Gaza City's al-Sabra neighbourhood killed several people, including children, as they slept. More than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed since a so-called ceasefire took effect in October 2025.

sources.title: A father’s agony after an Israeli air strike hits Gaza apartment

title: Will Ethiopia’s neighbours intervene as Tigray war escalates?
summary: Ethiopian federal forces have entered the Tigrayan capital Mekelle after nearly two weeks of fighting that has effectively ended the 2022 Pretoria ceasefire, but the TPLF-led rebel alliance has withdrawn to the countryside vowing to fight on, and reports of Eritrean troops entering northern Tigrayan towns add a dangerous regional dimension. Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia, wary of Abiy Ahmed's push for Red Sea access and the Renaissance Dam, met at a summit in New Alamein on October 4, though this is not a formal military alliance. Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats on October 1, and Eritrea severed ties; analysts say whether regional rivals intervene may depend on the TPLF keeping federal forces tied down in Tigray.

title: Kenyan patient suspected of Ebola infection tests negative
summary: A 20-year-old Kenyan man suspected of having Ebola after travelling from the DRC through Uganda tested negative in preliminary results, days after Kenya reported its first-ever Ebola case, a patient who died in Nairobi. Kenya is the fourth country to record a case linked to the DRC epidemic, the second-largest on record, which has killed at least 4,205 people; no vaccine exists for the Bundibugyo strain behind it. The first case exposed lapses in Kenya's border screening.

sources.title: Kenyan patient suspected of Ebola infection tests negative

title: Israel kills or wounds Palestinian every 90 minutes in Gaza since ceasefire
summary: Israeli attacks have killed or wounded a Palestinian in Gaza every 90 minutes on average since the October 2025 ceasefire, according to Islamic Relief, which counts at least 1,454 killed, including at least 320 children, and more than 5,000 wounded. Gaza's Health Ministry reports 1,471 killed since the ceasefire and at least 74,254 since October 2023. The charity says Israel has used the Yellow Line to push Palestinians out of 65 percent of Gaza while blocking shelter materials, fuel and medical supplies.

sources.title: Israel kills or wounds Palestinian every 90 minutes in Gaza since ceasefire

title: Tories overstate net zero cost by nearly £500bn in apparent spreadsheet error
summary: Kemi Badenoch's Conservative conference policy document, The Right Way, overstated the cost of net zero by nearly £500bn, apparently because a spreadsheet tally double-counted a row of totals. It claimed the Climate Change Committee estimated its route to net zero would cost £957bn, but the figures in the CCC report total £478bn, and the committee's latest analysis puts the cost at about £110bn, or 0.2% of GDP. The figure was used to justify the Conservatives' decision to scrap the 2050 net zero target; the error was spotted by Carbon Brief.

sources.title: Tories overstate net zero cost by nearly £500bn in apparent spreadsheet error

title: Second UK health body drops Israeli drug firm after activist pressure
summary: The Royal College of Pharmacy has dropped Teva UK, the British arm of Israeli drugmaker Teva Pharmaceuticals, as sponsor and exhibitor at its annual conference, following the Royal College of Nursing's decision last week to cut ties, both after pressure from pro-Palestine campaigners. The college cited a "due diligence review" of Teva activities that did not align with its values; campaigners are urging other royal colleges to follow, while Teva said healthcare should not become "politicised".

sources.title: Second UK health body drops Israeli drug firm after activist pressure

title: Revealed: the ‘black box’ wastewater trade that rakes in millions for UK utility companies
summary: An investigation found UK water companies made more than £340m in revenue last year by accepting industrial and commercial wastewater into sewage works that experts say are not designed to remove most chemicals, leaving pollutants to pass into rivers, seas and farmland. An annual 608bn litres of such wastewater enters sewage works under permits issued and enforced by the water companies themselves, with no direct role for environmental regulators; an industry expert said the companies had "a financial incentive to accept far more toxic material than they should".

sources.title: Revealed: the ‘black box’ wastewater trade that rakes in millions for UK utility companies

title: Firmus pulls biggest ASX float since Telstra amid investor doubt about datacentre company
summary: Firmus Technologies scrapped what was set to be the biggest ASX listing since Telstra in 1997 after investor demand for its AI datacentre business failed to materialise, amid scepticism over its anticipated $44bn valuation for a startup with just two small operational sites. The company, backed by Nvidia and Blackstone and seeking to raise $7bn, will now pursue private capital, after CDC this week also ended a touted $73bn deal with it.

sources.title: Firmus pulls biggest ASX float since Telstra amid investor doubt about datacentre company

title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues
summary: Egyptian journalists plan a protest in Cairo this weekend after six journalists from the independent factchecking platform Matsadaash were charged with terrorism offences, accused of producing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood. All six told lawyers they were tortured and forced to film false confessions, which police deny; colleagues see the case as part of a broader escalation by the authorities against independent media.

sources.title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues

title: Israel promotes film that mimics NAZA documentary
summary: Israeli embassies are promoting NAZA: The Real Story, an online film mimicking NAZA, the Guardian-produced documentary by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor on Israel's mass killings of civilians in Gaza, in an attempt to counter its findings. The rival film's website initially falsely presented itself as the real documentary's page and claims an implausible 42m views; Israel's government, which has announced plans to strip Abraham and Szor of their citizenship for treason, awarded the rival film-makers a certificate of appreciation.

title: Ethiopia launches drone attack against Eritrean troops who crossed into Tigray
summary: Ethiopian government drones struck Eritrean troops who crossed into Tigray and reached the town of Adigrat, raising the risk that Ethiopia's renewed internal conflict could trigger an all-out regional war. The incursion follows a TPLF offensive launched on 23 September and comes amid Eritrean fears of an Ethiopian invasion to gain Red Sea access, with prime minister Abiy Ahmed saying Ethiopia needs it and state media claiming historical rights to the Eritrean port of Assab.

sources.title: Ethiopia launches drone attack against Eritrean troops who crossed into Tigray

title: Florida judge allows lawsuit against Shah of Iran’s alleged ‘chief torturer’ to move forward
summary: A Florida federal judge rejected a bid by Parviz Sabeti, the alleged former head of the Shah of Iran's secret police Savak, to halt a torture lawsuit brought by three former political prisoners, refusing to strictly enforce the statute of limitations. Sabeti, who denies involvement in torture, could now face civil claims under the Torture Victim Protection Act as early as next year.

sources.title: Florida judge allows lawsuit against Shah of Iran’s alleged ‘chief torturer’ to move forward

title: U.S. Lawmakers Launch Sexual Abuse Probe of Youth Sports Giant AAU
summary: Bipartisan leaders of the House Energy and Commerce Committee launched an inquiry into the Amateur Athletic Union over its handling of child sexual abuse allegations, citing reporting by ProPublica and The Washington Post that found the group, with some 760,000 athletes and coaches, has become a haven for coaches suspected of abuse, does not offer the abuse prevention training it claims, and has suppressed allegations. The committee, which investigated the Larry Nassar scandal in 2018, demanded a briefing from AAU president Jo Mirza by Oct. 21 and data on abuse allegations and disciplined coaches.

sources.title: U.S. Lawmakers Launch Sexual Abuse Probe of Youth Sports Giant AAU

title: Club Med, a Disney Cruise and an Exploding Starship: SpaceX Used Bystander Videos to Track Falling Debris
summary: A SpaceX report obtained by ProPublica from the FAA via a public records request shows the company relied on bystander videos, including from Disney and Royal Caribbean cruise ships and a Club Med resort, to track debris after Starship's seventh test flight exploded over the Caribbean, suggesting its own tracking was incomplete. The FAA redacted most of the reports on flights 7, 8 and 9 and withheld SpaceX's estimates of where debris fell, leaving unclear how close airplanes came to it, even as the FAA nearly doubled pre-launch no-fly zones and SpaceX seeks up to 76 Starship launches a year from Cape Canaveral.

sources.title: Club Med, a Disney Cruise and an Exploding Starship: SpaceX Used Bystander Videos to Track Falling Debris

title: American Academy of Pediatrics Renews Call for Ban on Raw Milk
summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics renewed its call for a nationwide ban on the sale and distribution of raw milk and other unpasteurized dairy, warning of serious risks particularly for children, as consumption has grown to more than 10 million Americans and outbreaks have hit nine states in the past two years. The updated statement, which also cites avian influenza contamination, follows ProPublica reporting and comes as Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has championed raw milk rather than curbing it.

sources.title: American Academy of Pediatrics Renews Call for Ban on Raw Milk

title: Pete Hegseth’s Military of the Future: Defined by AI and an Utter Lack of Oversight
summary: War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an Autonomous Warfare Command, a four-star combatant command for AI-enabled robotic warfare to be established by October 1, 2027, and "Project Meridian," a 120-day study of future warfare led by Elon Musk, Newt Gingrich and Anduril founder Palmer Luckey. Former defense officials and contracting experts warn the command's acquisition powers are designed to bypass oversight and invite waste and fraud, while Meridian puts contractors with billions in Pentagon deals, including on the Golden Dome missile defense project, in charge of planning the military's future.

sources.title: Pete Hegseth’s Military of the Future: Defined by AI and an Utter Lack of Oversight

title: Armed Border Agents Arrest Protesters, Bulldoze 200-Year-Old Tree to Build Border Wall
summary: Around 150 Border Patrol agents raided a protest encampment on private land in Lochiel, Arizona, arresting at least 10 demonstrators and bulldozing a 200-year-old cottonwood that tree sitters had occupied since July to block construction of Trump's $50 billion border wall through the San Rafael Valley wildlife corridor. About 50 protesters remain in a standoff, and another activist has occupied the last cottonwood in the wall's path on the Mexico side. The raid followed a federal court injunction halting wall construction in the Big Bend area of Texas.

sources.title: Armed Border Agents Arrest Protesters, Bulldoze 200-Year-Old Tree to Build Border Wall

title: Between record debt and high school protests, France's situation draws global attention
summary: France's high school protest movement, set against a debt crisis, is drawing unusually strong international coverage. In the United States, debt tensions have dominated economic headlines, with Wall Street seeing France as proof of the failure of a country addicted to government spending, while riot footage has circulated widely on far-right MAGA social media channels and fueled xenophobic rhetoric among international far-right leaders.

sources.title: Between record debt and high school protests, France's situation draws global attention

title: Gaza rescuers say Israeli fire kills seven
summary: Gaza's civil defense said seven people were killed in separate Israeli strikes on Thursday, October 8, six of them in Gaza City, while the Israeli army said three of the victims were "military operatives." Hamas denied Israeli claims it uses Gaza hospitals for military activities. Since a ceasefire was declared in October last year, Israeli forces have killed at least 1,450 people in Gaza, according to the health ministry, which puts the war's total toll at more than 74,200.

sources.title: Gaza rescuers say Israeli fire kills seven

title: 'Trump dividend': Can promising voters a check help win an election?
summary: In an opinion piece, the author examines Donald Trump's promise, made since September 10, of a $5,000 "Trump Dividend" check to all adult citizens if Republicans keep control of both chambers in the November 3 midterm elections. The author calls it a legal but corrupt pact that would add $1.25 trillion to US public debt and is unlikely to be paid, since the House is very likely to swing to the Democrats, but argues it could still have a significant electoral impact, citing research on a similar 2006 pledge by Silvio Berlusconi.

sources.title: 'Trump dividend': Can promising voters a check help win an election?

title: France struggles to reassure financial markets as Asian investors fuel distrust
summary: French Economy Minister Roland Lescure is touring global financial centers to reassure investors about France's finances and its ability to pass the 2027 budget, if necessary, by executive order, as Asian funds are already turning away from France. After meeting about a dozen banks and asset managers in London on October 8, he pledged "We're going to use whatever it takes," and will discuss easing bond market tensions with EU counterparts, although any European Central Bank intervention is ruled out at this stage.

sources.title: France struggles to reassure financial markets as Asian investors fuel distrust

title: Pro-Iran groups behind foiled attack on Bank of America in Paris, FBI finds
summary: The homemade bomb that French teenagers tried to light outside Bank of America's Paris branch on the night of March 27 was orchestrated by pro-Iran groups, according to FBI findings shared with French anti-terrorism judges. The alleged mastermind, an Iraqi national arrested in Turkey, is suspected of orchestrating 18 attacks or planned attacks on European soil between March and May against American or Jewish targets, in response to the US-Israeli military offensive against Iran launched in February. The minors said they were recruited for a few hundred euros.

sources.title: Pro-Iran groups behind foiled attack on Bank of America in Paris, FBI finds

title: Macron tasks Michelin and BMW chiefs with forging a deal on European preference in the automotive sector
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron informally asked Michelin CEO Florent Menegaux and BMW supervisory board chairman Nicolas Peter on September 3 to narrow the gap between the French and German automotive sectors over European preference. At issue is a minimum local content requirement for subsidized cars, which France has pushed and which became part of the European Commission's "Industrial Accelerator Act" proposal presented on March 4.

sources.title: Macron tasks Michelin and BMW chiefs with forging a deal on European preference in the automotive sector

title: French presidential election: 'The far right and radical left remain highly fragile, as they face contradictions that are hard to overcome'
summary: In an opinion piece, the author argues that France's far right and radical left remain fragile seven months before the presidential election. title: Arrest warrant issued for Eduardo Bolsonaro – judge revoked his passport

title: Fon iddiaları: İki gazeteci ifadeye çağrıldı; iki gazeteci için de gözaltı kararı verildi
summary: İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, fon soruşturmasına ilişkin "kamuoyunu yanıltıcı nitelikle" açıklamalar yaptıkları gerekçesiyle gazeteciler İsmail Saymaz, Murat Ağırel ve Şaban Sevinç'in şüpheli sıfatıyla ifadelerinin alınmasına, ardından Sevinç ve Sözcü gazetesi editörü Mustafa Balcı hakkında gözaltı kararı verdi. Süreç, Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat'ın 7 Ekim'de Sözcü televizyonundaki yayın nedeniyle Saymaz ve Ağırel hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunmasıyla başladı. Bolat, 37,8 milyon liralık aile tasarrufunu iki yıl önce yatırdığını belirterek "400 koydu, 800 aldı ifadesi koskoca bir yalandır" dedi; Bakan Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş da kendisine yönelik iddiaları "yalan ve iftira" olarak nitelendirdi.

title: 'Cesur ve yaratıcı': Nobel Edebiyat Ödülü Kanadalı Şair Anne Carson'a verildi
summary: Nobel Edebiyat Ödülü, "klasik gelenekle eğlenceli bir diyalog kurarak çağdaş edebiyat için yeni biçimler yaratan" eserleri nedeniyle 76 yaşındaki Kanadalı şair Anne Carson'a verildi. Bu yılın bilim ödüllerinde Kimya Ödülü, yaşamın moleküler asimetrisi (kiralite) gizemine çözüm getiren Henri B. Kagan ve Kenso Soai'ye; Fizik Ödülü, Güney Kutbu'ndaki IceCube nötrino gözlemevine öncülük eden Francis Halzen'a; Tıp Ödülü ise beyin devrelerini ışıkla kontrol etmeyi sağlayan optogenetik çalışmaları nedeniyle Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann ve Georg Nagel'e verildi.

title: İran, 7 Ekim saldırıları sonrası caydırıcılık stratejisini nasıl değiştirdi?
summary: BBC Farsça'nın analizine göre, Hamas'ın 7 Ekim 2023 saldırılarının ardından geçen üç yılda Esad yönetiminin devrilmesi, Hamas ve Hizbullah'ın ağır darbe alması ve İran'ın İsrail ve ABD ile doğrudan savaşa girmesi, Tahran'ın müttefik gruplara dayanan "stratejik derinlik" yaklaşımının savaşı İran topraklarından uzak tutmakta başarısız olduğunu gösterdi. title: ABD ve Lübnan insanlığa karşı suç işlemekten aranan Suriyeli generali neden 'koruyor'?
summary: BBC ve NPR'ın ortak araştırmasına göre, insanlığa karşı suçlardan aranan ve Suriye'nin kimyasal silah programını denetleyen eski general Bassam el Hassan, Esad rejiminin çöküşünden bu yana FBI'ın da dahil olduğu bir anlaşmayla Lübnan'da ABD ve Lübnan yetkililerince korunuyor ve finanse ediliyor. Bunun karşılığı, Hassan'ın 2012'de Suriye'de kaçırılan Amerikalı gazeteci Austin Tice hakkında bilgi vermesi; ancak soruşturmada kayda değer ilerleme görülmedi. Suriye'nin yeni hükümeti Hassan'ın iadesini istiyor; FBI yorum yapmayı reddetti.
